cultural.vision_reason: A hand-woven strip-woven cotton wrapper (Keta cloth) with narrow-strip construction and weft-float geometric motifs is a classic Ewe textile form from the Volta Region of Ghana. This matches the claimed Ewe ethnicity well.

physical.title: wrapper; textile
physical.summary: Wrapper (Keta cloth), formed of 20 strips of hand-woven cotton, hand-sewn together along the selvages, with a standard warp pattern but with varying weft float designs. All the cotton is industrial European thread of four colours: white, red, yellow and two shades of blue. The warp pattern uses a dark blue background with one stripe of light blue and six white lines. The weft-faced patterns use a second pair of heddles, and (with a few exceptions) a standard block composed of dark blue, white, red and yellow. These are usually placed as pairs, between which are discontinuous weft float motifs in yellow. The warp ends have been hand-sewn with a hem.
